correctness.rationale: An exact change to the two scaling log-ratios converts each uniform-marginal half step into affine overrelaxation toward the unique conditional minimizer of a log-cosh profile. For 0<omega<2, the strict decrease of the globally coercive, strictly convex log-sum-exp potential makes every compact-level-set cluster point its unique critical point. The actual coupling (not just projective ratios) converges because its logarithmic common scale satisfies an exact forced affine recurrence with coefficient (1-omega)^2<1. For omega=2 the potential is exactly invariant under both conditional reflections, while omega>2 makes it nondecreasing; nonoptimal initial states cannot converge. A standalone example checker was run after assembly. Finite tests are explicitly not a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The 2015 archive-era source establishes entropic diagonal scaling, the 2017 overrelaxation paper gives an adaptive global method and local constant-parameter SOR, and the 2020/2021 fixed-parameter paper gives only the Birkhoff-limited sufficient interval 0<omega<2/(1+Lambda(K)) for global convergence. The candidate instead proves the exact all-start unsafeguarded interval (0,2) on the natural balanced 2x2 family, including the excluded omega=2 boundary and convergence of unnormalized transport couplings. Targeted database and published alias searches found no implication-equivalent statement; residual terminology risk remains.
residual_risks: An older nonlinear block-SOR or matrix-balancing treatment might contain the exact uniform 2x2 all-start result under different terminology.
Existing adaptive Sinkhorn algorithms are valid for broader dimensions; the present result does not claim general superiority or speedup.
Proof depends on strictly positive kernels and equal two-atom marginals; near-zero kernel entries can make convergence slow.

value.rationale: Uniform two-point entropic OT is the smallest nontrivial case of a widely deployed diagonal scaling algorithm, and relaxation close to two is practically natural when unrelaxed scaling is slow. Existing general fixed-parameter global guarantees can shrink nearly to omega=1 for badly coupled kernels, while local theory allows every omega<2. The theorem closes that actual global/local gap exactly for the natural minimal family, proves the sharp boundary, and provides a simple strict Lyapunov mechanism and a dramatic K=[[100,1],[1,100]] example; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or a table lookup.
